newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower, off day's lows.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower, off day's lows.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures closed lower to sharply lower, weighed down by falling cash hog and belly prices, but declines were pared late by local short covering, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.600 to 0.050 cent per lb lower with June off 0.500 at 83.500 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.900 to 1.950 cent lower with July off 1.150 at 87.700 cents.

A lack of follow-through selling, after futures posted 2-1/2 week lows and fell through 20-day moving averages, prompted local short covering near the close, traders noted. Futures had been under pressure early as fund liquidation and general selling triggered sell stops, they said.

Selling from the start reflected the weak tone to cash markets. Pork cutout values fell again Friday and packers bid lower for cash hogs Monday and were seen dropping bids again Tuesday as margins remained deep into the red, they said.
USDA quoted pork cut-out values down $0.79 to $0.82 per cwt Friday and at midday Monday, central carlot prices on hams were steady to $1.00 lower and bellies, $3-$5 lower.
The April runup in pork prices following Taiwan's pork ban boosted values to a level that stifled domestic and foreign demand for pork, they added.
"High prices slashed pork interest," one trader said.

Local short covering partially offset the early selling by R.J. O'Brien in June and July. Dean Witter and Cargill Investor Services also sold June early, traders said. LIT division of First Options sold August while Rand Financials bought late, pit sources said.

In hog options, commission houses lightly sold June 78 to 82 puts and July 81 to 82 puts early. Locals lightly bought June 84 to 87 calls late following the rally from lows in futures, pit sources added.
Pork belly futures also tumbled for sharp losses early before losses were pared by local short covering.

Carryover selling prompted by the weak tone to cash bellies and technical weakness touched off early sell stops. Futures fell to two-week lows on light fund pressure but the selling lacked follow through and local short covering pared losses late, traders said.
Cash belly prices declined another $3 to $5 per cwt Monday with 14-16 lb bellies falling to $78 to $80, $10 to $12 down from the recent high.
Delivery concerns also weighed on May during the day with first notice day Monday. Pit and floor talk centered around 150 to 175 deliveries, they added.
R.J. O'Brien, Smith Barney and Refco sold July after light initial buying by Rand Financials, pit sources added.
